paragraphs: Here's what I hear in this one, friend. The master hands out the talents "each according to his own ability" (Matthew 25:15), so nobody gets handed more than they can carry. And listen to the praise. The five-talent servant and the two-talent servant get the exact same words, "Well done, good and faithful servant!" (Matthew 25:21, 23). I think the master cared less about who ended up with the biggest pile and more about who was faithful with what he got.

Now look at the one-talent servant, who says, "I was afraid" (Matthew 25:25). I bet burying the money felt like the safe move, and friend, I get it. But the master answers him, "You wicked, lazy servant!" (Matthew 25:26). I spent years buried in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, buried is not the same as safe. It's just dusty.

The master was gone "a long time" before he came back (Matthew 25:19), so this was never a sprint. Whatever you've been handed, baker, put it to work today and don't wait for some perfect Monday. Fear says hide it, and faithfulness says use it. Jesus isn't done teaching yet, so stick with me.
